study: PHONE_CONTROLLER C2 (Android): the user's controller on a real phone
kind: actual device observation (the user played; adb over Wi-Fi recorded the input side)

phone.adbWifi: 192.168.0.52:5555 (adb tcpip while on USB, then the phone moved into the controller)

apk.build: debug local.ntsd.port from the MENU_MEMORY gate mm-2; the Android sources equal main (only NTSDiOS and NTSDWeb changed since 340b1a64)

recorder: scratchpad watch.sh: dumpsys input and getevent -pl on every input-device change, getevent -lt, logcat -v threadtime, pidof local.ntsd.port every 2 s

controller.name: Razer Razer Kishi V2
controller.correction: C0 identified the device from the photo as a Backbone One (USB-C); the device reports itself as a Razer Kishi V2

hidNodes.abs: X Y Z RZ GAS BRAKE 0..255 flat 15 (rest 0x80); HAT0X HAT0Y -1..1
hidNodes.keys: BTN_SOUTH(GAMEPAD) EAST C NORTH WEST Z TL TR TL2 TR2 SELECT START MODE THUMBL THUMBR
the same 15 gamepad buttons, no axes

hidNodes.name: Razer Razer Kishi V2 Consumer Control
hidNodes.keys: VOLUMEDOWN VOLUMEUP POWER MENU SLEEP BACK HOMEPAGE APPSELECT

androidInputDevices.motionRanges: X Y Z RZ -1..1 flat 0.118; LTRIGGER RTRIGGER GAS BRAKE 0..1; HAT_X HAT_Y -1..1

timeline.clock: Mac CEST (+02:00); logcat lines are the phone's local time, one hour ahead

runs.note: controller attached at 18:52:54, during the run
the played test, about 4 min 40 s

controllerAttached: attached between the 18:51:28 and 18:51:46 samples, removed by 18:52:28

rawEventsOnController.note: event counts include presses and releases over the whole recording; the d-pad arrives as hat axes, which the host's hat path takes over the stick

findings: The controller works in the game as joystick 1: the user played run 3 with it (stick, d-pad, buttons).

Inference from NTSDAndroidGamepads.probe (first two ids with SOURCE_GAMEPAD, ids ascending) and the device list: the game is also given id 5, the controller's button-only input2 node, which sent no event, as joystick 2; a second gamepad would not get that slot. The game's joystick count is not logged on Android.

Closing run 3: libc 'Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1 (SEGV_MAPERR), fault addr 0x0 in tid 21473 (Jit thread pool), pid 21467 (local.ntsd.port)' 94 ms after the window became invisible, then Zygote 'Process 21467 exited cleanly (0)'; no tombstone, no error dialog; runs 1 and 2 closed without it. The host's onDestroy calls Foundation.exit(0) while ART's threads run; recorded, not studied.
